summary: Over the last 4 weeks training volume has been moderate but inconsistent, with notable gaps in running (only one run recorded) and swimming while cycling has dominated. Sleep is chronically short — most nights sitting at 3–4 hours rather than the recommended 7–8 — and body battery scores are persistently low, signalling accumulated fatigue that needs addressing before the Half Oceanman today and the Treviso 10K in 8 days. The single run on 25 Sep showed a very high HR of 169 bpm at a modest 6:15/km pace, suggesting running-specific fitness needs careful rebuilding rather than aggressive interval work in the near term.
suggestions: Today is race day for the Half Oceanman 5,000 m swim — focus entirely on warm-up, race execution, and post-race fuelling; avoid any additional training load whatsoever.

With the Treviso 10K only 8 days away, treat the next 8 days as a mini-taper: keep all sessions short and easy, avoid high-intensity intervals (especially the Wk16 6×800 m session on Oct 6), and prioritise sleep above 7 hours per night to allow body battery to recover from its chronically low state.

Chronic sleep deprivation (averaging ~5.5 hrs/night across 4 weeks) is the single biggest limiter visible in your data — address this immediately by targeting a minimum 7 hours; without this, no training prescription will yield the intended adaptation.

Running fitness appears underdeveloped relative to the 5:45/km Treviso target — your only run in 4 weeks was at 169 bpm average for 6:15/km, so arrive at the 10K start line fresh rather than chasing fitness with hard sessions this week.

From Wk17 onwards (post-Treviso), prioritise re-introducing structured running at 2–3 sessions per week with one quality session and one long run, as the marathon and Ironman run targets require a sustained build that is currently absent from recent training.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Evening session — 6×800 m intervals at 4:55–5:10/km, 90 min total
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with 30–35 min very easy jog at 6:45–7:15/km — no intervals; this is race-week prep for Treviso 10K on Oct 10.
proposed_changes.reason: Running a hard interval session 4 days before the Treviso 10K risks accumulated leg fatigue and a poor race result; easy aerobic running keeps legs ticking over without adding stress.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Pool Swim (Tuesday) — 2 km+ at ≤2:30/100 m, 60 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Shorten to 1,200–1,500 m easy technique-focused swim at comfortable effort — no hard sets; reduce total training stress in Treviso race week.
proposed_changes.reason: Maintaining swim volume in the days before a 10K run race adds unnecessary fatigue when the priority discipline this week is running.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Gym / Strength — 60 min full strength session
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Reduce to 20–25 min very light activation only: bodyweight single-leg calf raises, hip mobility, and core breathing — skip all heavy loading 2 days before Treviso 10K.
proposed_changes.reason: Heavy strength work 48 hours before a race leaves muscles sore and legs heavy; a brief activation session maintains neuromuscular readiness without fatigue cost.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk16 Evening session — 90 min Z2 endurance spin at 128–177 W
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip entirely — no cycling session 2 days before Treviso 10K; legs need to be fully fresh.
proposed_changes.reason: Adding a 90-min bike session two days out from the 10K race will accumulate residual muscular fatigue that compromises race-day running performance.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk17 Evening session — 6×800 m intervals at 4:55–5:10/km, 90 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with 4×800 m at 5:00–5:15/km with 90-sec jog recovery, total ~45 min — reduced volume as first quality run session in the post-race recovery week following Treviso.
proposed_changes.reason: Jumping straight back to 6 reps of hard intervals the Thursday after a 10K race risks overloading underdeveloped run fitness; starting with 4 reps is a safer re-introduction.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk17 Long Run — 17.6 km at 6:15–6:45/km, 180 min
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Cap at 12–13 km at 6:30–7:00/km (approx 80–90 min) — do not attempt the full planned distance the week after racing the Treviso 10K.
proposed_changes.reason: Given only one run in the past 4 weeks and a 10K race on Oct 10, jumping to a 17.6 km long run 8 days later is a large spike in running load that increases injury risk significantly.
